claim.claim-text: 1. A method for operating a magnetically actuated switch assembly (50) to perform a low energy test pulse, the switch assembly (50) including a fixed contact (52) and a movable contact (54), the method comprising:

energizing a magnetic actuator (58) to move the moveable contact (54) against the bias of at least one spring (66, 78) coupled to the movable contact (54) towards the fixed contact (52) to make contact therebetween, wherein AC current conducts across a gap (56) formed between the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) as the moveable contact (54) is moved toward the fixed contact (52) and before the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) make contact; and reversing the magnetic actuator (58) to move the movable contact (54) away from the fixed contact (52) at least under the bias of the at least one spring (66, 78) so that the amount of time that the current conducts between the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) is about one fundamental frequency cycle, and preferably, about one-half of one fundamental frequency cycle of the current, wherein reversing the magnetic actuator (58) occurs at a time so that when the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) begin conducting an applied voltage on the switch assembly (50) is at or near a peak of the voltage wave so that the current is symmetric.
2. The method according to claim 1 wherein the voltage on the switch assembly (50) that is at or near the peak of the voltage wave is at a 90° voltage angle.
3. The method according to claim 1 wherein the contacts (52, 54) are part of a vacuum interrupter.

4. The method according to claim 3 wherein the current is a fault current in a medium voltage power distribution network (10) and the vacuum interrupter is part of a recloser (24) in the power distribution network (10).

5. A method for performing a reclosing fault testing operation in a power distribution network (10) using a vacuum interrupter including a fixed contact (52) and a movable contact (54), the method comprising:

energizing a magnetic actuator (58) to move the movable contact (54) against the bias of at least one spring (66, 78) coupled to the movable contact (54) towards the fixed contact (52) to make contact therebetween, wherein AC fault current conducts across a gap (56) formed between the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) as the moveable contact (54) is moved toward the fixed contact (52) and before the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) make contact; and reversing the magnetic actuator (58) to move the movable contact (54) away from the fixed contact (52) at least under the assistance of the bias of the at least one spring (66, 78) so that the amount of time that the current conducts between the movable contact (54) and the fixed contact (52) is about one fundamental frequency cycle, and preferably, about one-half of one fundamental frequency cycle of the fault current.
6. The method according to claim 1 or claim 5 wherein the one fundamental frequency cycle of current is about 16.7 ms for 60 Hz.

7. The method according to claim 6 wherein the time that the contacts (52, 54) begin conducting to the time the contacts (52, 54) will withstand voltage when the current goes to zero is about three-quarters of the one fundamental frequency cycle time.
8. The method according to claim 1 or claim 5 wherein the at least one spring is a larger open spring (66) and a smaller compliance spring (78).
9. The method according to claim 8 wherein the open spring (66) is wrapped around a cylindrical housing (60) and the compliance spring (78) is provided within the housing (60).

10. The method according to claim 9 wherein the magnetic actuator (58) includes a stationary core (86) having a coil and a movable core (92) that moves towards the stationary core (86) when the actuator (58) is energized, and wherein reversing the magnetic actuator (58) comprises de-energizing the magnetic actuator (58) or reversing an applied voltage on the magnetic actuator (58).
11. A magnetically actuated switch assembly (50) having a low energy pulse test capability, the switch assembly (50) comprising:
12. The magnetically actuated switch assembly (50) according to claim 11 wherein the one fundamental frequency cycle of current is about 16.7 ms for 60 Hz.

13. The magnetically actuated switch assembly (50) according to claim 12 wherein the time that the contacts (52, 54) begin conducting to the time the contacts (52, 54) will withstand voltage when the current goes to zero is about three-quarters of the one fundamental frequency cycle time.
14. The magnetically actuated switch assembly (50) according to claim 11 wherein the voltage on the switch assembly (50) that is at or near the peak of the voltage wave is at a 90° voltage angle.
